page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon processor providing 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Hardware cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache. System memory totals 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains no bundled local storage and includes zero integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations position the instance firmly in the middle tier of general compute performance. In stress-ng, it posts 1,839.48 in single-core and 15,060.78 in multi-core metrics, matched by a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,239.0. Memory subsystems deliver 84.64 GB/sec read and 43.14 GB/sec write throughput for large blocks, supporting 14.19 million Redis SET operations per second and 12.34 GB/sec in static web serving. While instruction extensions like AVX-512 VNNI support vector operations, single-threaded throughput shows lower relative output, reflected in bottom-quartile marks for gzip compression and single-threaded bzip3 decompression.

Without local NVMe disks, I/O performance relies on attached network storage volumes, which should be accounted for when provisioning throughput-heavy applications. The 4:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio yields a cost-efficient profile for steady, multi-threaded enterprise workloads that require balanced resources without the overhead of specialized hardware accelerators. n2-standard-16 is suited for multi-tier web application servers, relational databases with moderate memory requirements, microservice backends, CI/CD compilation tasks, and Redis caching tiers.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual instance configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, running on an Intel Xeon processor at 2.8 GHz using the x86_64 architecture. Offering an even 4.0 GB of memory per core across 8 physical cores, the instance provides steady middle-tier compute and memory throughput across industry benchmarks such as PassMark and Geekbench. It includes instruction sets like AVX-512 VNNI, though it lacks integrated GPUs and local disk storage, necessitating network-attached storage for persistence. Memory bandwidth is consistent, recording 84.64 GB/sec uncached reads and sustaining over 14 million Redis SET operations per second, although single-threaded compression performance ranks in lower quartiles. The instance represents an efficient infrastructure choice for standard enterprise backends, CI/CD build environments, relational databases, and static or dynamic web application serving.
